newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Russian YUKOS plans stake in Lithuania terminal.
newsitem.headline: Russian YUKOS plans stake in Lithuania terminal.

text.p: Russia's second largest oil firm YUKOS plans to take a 10 percent stake in Lithuania's Klaipedos Nafta oil terminal and to ship two to three million tonnes of oil through it a year, a company spokesman said on Wednedsay.
"There have been some talks between our company and Yukos but any agreement between the two parties has to be approved by the government," a Klaipedos Nafta official told Reuters.
He gave no figures for the sale but newspaper Lietuvos rytas said the stake had a four million litas nominal value.
The terminal is currently upgrading its facilities with the help of a $40 million loan from Dutch ABN Amro.
It has an annual capactiy of some eight million tonnes.
The terminal is 51 percent owned by the company Klaipedos Terminalas and 49 percent by the U.S. firm Lancaster Steel Inc, owned by two Lithuanian brothers.
YUKOS is the parent company of Yuganskneftegaz.
